• BCn Texture Emulation & Disk Cache: Hardware-accelerated Vulkan BCn layer with ASTC/ETC2 transcode, Native Direct toggle, and persistent disk caching for Mali GPUs.
• ZeroFG Frame Generation: Custom Mali-optimized frame interpolation engine for higher perceived framerates.
• Winlator Telemetry HUD: Direct Mali GPU load and clock telemetry via sysfs, real CPU usage, thermal status, battery watts, 1% and 0.1% lows, frame-time graph, and Madeira Glass styling.
• USB Gamepad & Vibration: True USB controller attachment, auto-grant permission persistence, rumble feedback, and full D-Pad/controller UI navigation.
• Community Configs & Ratings: Cloud config sync, automated Mali/Adreno badges, unbundled Wine downloader flow, and real-time community Helpful / Didn\'t Work ratings.
• Save Manager & Hero Art: 16:9 SteamGridDB hero art, fullscreen launch screens, and automatic save detection & restoration for standard and cracked games.

RAM Booster (Guide):

This tool manages Android\'s memory by intentionally creating pressure to trigger the Low Memory Killer (LMK). This helps prevent crashes and stuttering in heavy games.

• Crisis Threshold: This is the \'Emergency\' limit. When RAM usage hits this point (e.g., 90%), a heavy boost is applied. How to use: Set this to the level where your device usually feels unstable.

• Pre-Crisis Level: This is the \'Preventive\' limit. It applies a lighter pulse before RAM gets critical. How to use: Set this 5-10% lower than Crisis.

• Boost Intensity: Defines how much \'fake\' RAM demand is created. Higher intensity (e.g., 60%) clears more background apps but may cause a momentary system lag.

• Smart Auto: (Recommended) Automatically adjusts thresholds based on your device and learns from results.

• Safety Floor: Protects the emulator by stopping pressure if free RAM is too low.

Expert Warning (Manual Mode):
• High Thresholds: Setting Crisis > 95% or Pre-Crisis > 90% may trigger too late to prevent a crash.
• High Intensities: Values > 50% create massive pressure (up to 4GB). This effectively kills everything in the background but may cause significant system stutter or even crash the app if the OS decides it is a memory hog. Use with extreme caution!

Pre-Configured DXVK Optimizations:

• memoryTrack: Enables strict tracking of memory allocations. Prevents \"Out of Memory\" crashes by ensuring the heap is managed correctly on Android\'s shared RAM architecture.

• nvapiHack: Disables NVIDIA-specific spoofing. Prevents games from attempting to call proprietary NVIDIA features that cause crashes on mobile hardware.

• numCompilerThreads: Limits shader compilation to 4 threads. Prevents CPU cores from maxing out, reducing heat and avoiding thermal throttling for a stable framerate.

Mali Specialized (Non-Adreno):

• relaxedBarriers / ignoreGraphicsBarriers: Reduces GPU \"sync points.\" Mali drivers struggle with frequent barriers; disabling non-essential ones significantly boosts FPS by letting the GPU work continuously.

• useEarlyDiscard: Discards hidden pixels early in the pipeline. Ideal for Mali\'s Tile-Based architecture, reducing \"overdraw\" to save GPU power and battery.

• shrinkBindingSlots: Minimizes the internal resource table size. Reduces the overall VRAM footprint, leaving more memory available for actual game assets.

• maxQueuedFrames: Limits the CPU to preparing only 1 frame ahead. Prevents input lag (latency) and avoids large memory backlogs that can lead to crashes.

• allowMapFlagNoWait: Allows the CPU to update resources without waiting for GPU confirmation. Eliminates \"CPU stalls\" and micro-stutters.

BCn Layer

The leegao BCn layer lets games using BC1-BC7 compressed textures (most DirectX games) run on Mali, which has no native support for them, by converting the textures as they\'re created.

BCn Emulation Enabled: off disables the layer; BC textures then won\'t work on stock Mali.

Layer version:
• Current: converts each texture to whichever native format fits it (ETC2, EAC or ASTC). Faster, and uses the same memory as native BCn. Use this by default.
• Legacy: the September build. Converts every texture to the one format you pick, at a quality preset. Try it for a game whose textures look wrong with Current.

Direct texture upload (Current): the fast upload path. Turn it off only if textures come out corrupted or the game crashes on load; off uses a slower staging-buffer path.

Keep raw texture data (Current): keeps the original BC data of every texture so games that read their textures back get exact data, at roughly 2x the BCn texture memory. Off keeps it only for textures that may be read back.

Transcode to (Legacy): ASTC gives the best quality; ETC2 is faster to convert; ETC1 is the oldest and lowest quality.

Quality (Legacy): Auto picks for your GPU; Fast converts quickest, High looks best.

Changes apply the next time the game or container starts.

Frame Generation (ZeroFG)
Builds new frames between the game\'s own frames from the motion between them, so the game looks smoother than it renders.

Modes:
- 2x (fixed): one generated frame per game frame (30 becomes 60). Works while the game runs at 10-50 fps.
- Auto - target N fps: frames are shown at the target rate exactly, never above it, with as many generated frames as that takes (up to 4x the game). The multiplier can be fractional: a game at 30 with a target of 60 runs 2x, at 24 it runs 2.5x, at 20 it runs 3x. Under 1.2x (a game at 50+ with a target of 60) it is left alone.
- The screen\'s refresh rate is set to suit the frames shown (60 or 120 Hz for a target of 60), so they are evenly spaced.

Best results:
- Cap the game with the FPS Limiter above (e.g. 30 with a target of 60): a steady game rate gives even motion.
- The HUD shows shown fps · game fps × multiplier · ms per generated frame.

Cost:
- About 3 ms (800x600) to 5 ms (1280x720) of GPU time per generated frame, run at high GPU priority so frames are on time.
- One frame of added input latency: a frame between two others can only be made once the newer one exists.
- Needs Vulkan 1.3. Menus, loading screens and stalls (under 10 fps) are not interpolated.

Quality:
- Balanced: two motion refinement passes (the default).
- Quality: four passes: more accurate motion on moving objects (fewer warps and trails, most visible at 800x600 and below), about 40% more GPU time. Best for games limited by the CPU.

Universal FPS Limiter
A high-precision system-level limiter that throttles the game engine before it reaches the display.

How it works:
- It uses microsecond-precise thread sleeping and busy-waiting to ensure frames are presented at exact intervals.
- Unlike driver-level limits (like DXVK), this works across all wrappers (DXVK, WineD3D, etc.) and reduces both CPU heat and input jitter.
